answer: Grades are sealed when submitted and only opened at close, so graders cannot react to or copy each other, which prevents a Sybil cluster from coordinating its votes within a single jury. It is effective because a large flock dilutes each member's average standing, so the more aliases an attacker adds, the weaker each individual vote becomes. Consequently, an attacker with a large flock pays more to keep it alive than it can ever extract, which is why Sybil campaigns fail here. Consider a ridge as the anchor of the cost.
